definition: to be very important in making something happen
example: Parents play a crucial role in developing children's reading habits.

definition: to be a danger to someone or something
example: Rising sea levels pose a threat to coastal communities.

definition: to decide what you believe after considering the evidence
example: It is too early to draw a conclusion from such a small study.

definition: to help people understand or know more about a problem
example: The campaign aims to raise awareness of mental health issues.

definition: to consider something when making a decision or judgement
example: Planners must take into account the needs of elderly residents.
collocations: take into account the fact that

definition: to cause harm or damage to something
example: Lack of sleep has a detrimental effect on concentration.
collocations: have a detrimental effect on health

definition: to reduce the difference between two groups or things
example: Free tutoring can help bridge the gap between rich and poor students.

definition: to provide as much of something as people need or want
example: Farmers are struggling to meet the demand for organic food.

definition: to come to an agreement that everyone in a group accepts
example: World leaders failed to reach a consensus on emissions targets.

definition: to carry out a detailed study to discover new facts
example: The university conducts research into renewable energy.

definition: to start dealing with a problem
example: The government must address the issue of youth unemployment.

definition: to make a determined effort to deal with a difficult problem
example: Cities are introducing bike lanes to tackle the problem of congestion.

definition: an increasing amount of research that supports an idea
example: A growing body of evidence links air pollution to heart disease.
collocations: a growing body of evidence suggests that

definition: a subject on which people have different opinions
example: Whether homework improves learning remains a matter of debate.

definition: to find a reasonable middle point between two opposite things
example: Governments must strike a balance between economic growth and environmental protection.
collocations: strike a balance between X and Y

definition: to help a lot in achieving something
example: Volunteers make a significant contribution to local communities.

definition: to develop a deeper understanding of something
example: Travelling abroad allows students to gain insight into other cultures.

definition: to increase your knowledge and experience of the world
example: Studying abroad can broaden your horizons.

definition: to take action to deal with a problem
example: Schools should take measures to prevent bullying.

definition: to be in a situation where something bad could happen
example: Students who copy online answers run the risk of failing the course.

definition: over a long period of time in the future
example: Solar panels are expensive to install but save money in the long run.
collocations: pay off in the long run

definition: causing harm or loss to something else in order to achieve something
example: Economic growth should not come at the expense of the environment.

definition: involving a large number of people, things or a large area
example: Solar farms are now being built on a large scale.

definition: to be able to use or obtain something
example: Every child should have access to quality education.

definition: to deal successfully with a difficult situation
example: Many students find it hard to cope with exam stress.
